contradictions.detail: The listing states the car was previously sold on BaT in June 2023 ($27,000, BorisF to BMWNJ). The Carfax ownership quoted in comments shows owner 2 continuously from June 2015 to March 2026, with no change at June 2023. The seller says the sale went through and that Carfax is mistaken, but offers no document. This leaves the custody gap between 2023 and 2026, and who owned the car, unresolved.

critical_evidence.evidence: No DME scan or software-version printout. The engine-bay photo shows an apparently stock N55 bay with no visible piggyback, but that is not proof of stock software.
No injector or HPFP documentation. This is an N55, so the N54 HPFP and piezo concern is reduced, but the solenoid injectors still fail individually. The 20 Carfax entries are not itemised.
No electric water pump or thermostat record. At 13 years and 60k miles, the whole cooling job should be assumed due unless proven.
The car is a six-speed manual, so the relevant record is clutch or dual-mass flywheel history. None is mentioned.
E82 coupe with a glass sunroof, not a convertible. There is no top mechanism. Sunroof drains and dry footwells remain a PPI item.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: VIN, clean-title claim, Carfax summary with 20 service entries, cold-start, functions and imperfections videos, and paint-meter photos. The maintenance half is missing: no invoices for cooling, injectors, clutch or software. The 2023-2026 ownership record is also contradictory.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight paint, a clean-looking stock engine bay and a tidy underside. Tires carry 2022/2023 dates. Offsetting this are the replaced rear bumper with an undisclosed cause, the removed hitch, and no proof of age-related cooling or gasket work. Steering-wheel rim wear and slightly hazy headlight lenses are visible.

price_value.rationale: The current bid is meaningless in a reserve auction. A 135is 6MT in Le Mans Blue should hammer near or above the $16,914 fair-value mid, likely high teens to mid-$20ks. It sold for $27,000 in 2023. At expected money the price carries an uninsured cooling, gasket and clutch catch-up.

mission_fit.rationale: Manual and rear-drive, with a clear point of view and strong resale. However, it is a turbo N55 BMW, a family the buyer has deprioritised, with the same cooling-system weak points as his failing 335i. The no-contingency wire terms also limit flexibility.

logistics.rationale: Pennsylvania dealer, far from Carmel. Pre-auction inspections via a local shop or Lemon Squad are explicitly welcomed and shipping is offered. The car was originally CA-delivered, so smog is likely feasible. The PPI must fit within six days and the wire is due in 3 business days.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: the 135is, the top 1-Series spec, a six-speed manual, Le Mans Blue, Premium and Technology Packages, Shadowline trim, and an apparently stock car.

Oil leaks: oil filter housing gasket (belt contamination), valve cover, oil pan and the turbo oil feed lines
Turbo wastegate rattle at light throttle between 1,500 and 2,500 rpm, plus underboost codes
Clutch slip in a high-gear pull, DMF chatter at idle, and synchro feel when cold

Sunroof drains and dry footwells and trunk; FRM and Comfort Access function

evidence.mission_note: It meets the enthusiast brief on transmission, character and resale, but it is a turbo N55 BMW with the same cooling-system weak points as the failing 335i, which the buyer has deprioritised. It needs strong records to be the low-risk bridge he wants.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2013 135i coupe, photos confirm a six-speed manual 135is in Le Mans Blue with Shadowline trim, and the engine bay and underside look stock and clean in the captured photos. Tires carry 2022/2023 date codes, and Carfax shows 20 service entries and no reported damage. Observed issues are a replaced rear bumper cover of undisclosed cause, a removed trailer hitch, and a material conflict between the June 2023 BaT sale and the Carfax ownership timeline. The seller has answered that conflict only with an assertion. None of the model-critical items is documented: no DME scan proving stock software, no cooling-system or injector receipts, and no clutch or DMF history. Takata airbag recall completion is also unknown. Expected hammer for this spec is roughly $19k-$25k against a fair-value mid of $16,914. The car sold for $27,000 in 2023. The dealer invites pre-auction inspection, but the sale is non-contingent with a 3-day wire, so all verification must happen before Oct 20.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller via Contact Seller today. Request the full Carfax, the 2023-2026 title chain, itemised service invoices and an ISTA software and fault scan. In parallel, book a Lemon Squad or local BMW-specialist PPI in Douglassville before the Oct 20, 12:28 PM Pacific close.
